display.title: Episode 156: The Flickering Flame, Chapter 1 (Zos Chanukah)
display.summary_short: On the eighth night of Chanukah: 'good, better, best' and climbing the ranks of Tzivos Hashem, honoring Tati when he comes home, and Rabbi Yisrael Salanter finds a cobbler working late.
display.summary_long: Broadcast as the eighth Chanukah candle is lit. Uncle Yossi explains that adding a candle each night teaches maalin bakodesh, always going higher in holiness, and repeats his rhyme 'Good, better, best, don't sit down to rest.' Using the new Tzivos Hashem newsletter he shows how members earn points to rise from private to sergeant and all the way to general. After a festive Hakochainik march, Mitzvah Time turns to honoring Tati: greet him warmly after work, help with his coat and slippers, and do not disturb his supper. A caller wins by remembering to put away her toys, and a new board game, Target 613, is advertised. A yeshiva student leads the Shema. Story time teaches that we can learn from everyone and everything, as Rabbi Akiva learned from water dripping on a rock. Then a new story begins: Rabbi Yisrael Salanter, arriving in a town late at night, sees a light in a cobbler's window and wonders why the cobbler is still working. The lesson of the flickering flame is saved for next week.
display.lesson: Like the Chanukah lights, always go higher: good, better, best. And there is a lesson for us in everything we see.
